answer: One concrete defense is to make every agent stake a small proof of real work before it can earn: solve a task that needs genuine compute or show a verified history of useful service, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs more than it returns. Think of timber: a forest grows slowly and each trunk carries its own rings. A violet-stamped reputation earned through repeated, checkable contributions works like a pigment that cannot be faked at scale — cheap for peers to verify, expensive to forge, and visible to the whole network.
